messages:
mike: Quick ask — can someone run a quick parity bench for customer-acme VPC today? Need: 1) p99 latency + throughput for seq=1024 and seq=2048, 2) cold vs warmed KV cache, 3) fp16 vs 8-bit quant. Target model: redwood/guanaco-7b-instruct (quant variants ok). Running on 8xA100 bare-metal. TL;DR: are we within hosted profile numbers?

sara: I can take this. Do you have the Docker image tag + recommended runner config (batch, concurrency)? Also need the promptset and warmup script.

mike: image: registry.redwood.ai/inference:release-20260412. Config: batch_size=8, max_tokens=1024, concurrency=16, seq_lengths=[1024,2048]. Use prompt set at gs://acme/perf/promptset-v2. Warmup: 500 requests with prefix cache warming. Please capture p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.

sara: sg. I'll run on node-group `onprem-8a100` — planning a two-pass run (cold + warm). Command I'll use: ```python bench.py --image registry.redwood.ai/inference:release-20260412 --model guanaco-7b --batch 8 --concurrency 16 --seq 2048 --warmup 500 --quant fp16 --out perf-job-20260415-37.log``` Will post summary here when done.

raj: small ask — ensure KV cache is populated across all GPUs. Use the prefill tool: `./tools/prefill_kv.sh --model guanaco-7b --nodes 8 --prefix "The quick brown"`. Without that, a cold run can underreport steady-state throughput.

nora: FYI we saw a regression in the attention kernel after the newer CUDA driver on onprem clusters. If you hit spikes, set `KERNEL_OVERRIDE=attention_v2` in the env to force the fallback optimized path for quantized workloads.

sara: noted. Running both: (1) cold no prefill, (2) warm with prefill + KERNEL_OVERRIDE. Also comparing fp16 vs 8bit. ETA ~45m.

ops-bot: Job scheduled: perf-job-20260415-37 on cluster onprem-8a100. Logs: https://perf.redwood.ai/jobs/perf-job-20260415-37 :clock3: 

mike: thanks — please include per-token cost estimate (tokens/sec and estimated $/1M tokens) and a tiny table of p50/p95/p99 for each combo (seq, quant, cold/warm).

sara: results summary (posting short):
- seq=1024, fp16, cold: p99=220ms, tps=48, tokens/sec=38k
- seq=1024, fp16, warm: p99=130ms, tps=85, tokens/sec=67k
- seq=2048, fp16, warm: p99=400ms, tps=34, tokens/sec=56k
- seq=2048, 8bit, warm: p99=360ms, tps=38, tokens/sec=62k
CPU host spikes observed ~70% during decode. Raw logs: https://perf.redwood.ai/raw/perf-job-20260415-37.log (tagging @nora @raj)

nora: looks like 8bit yields slightly better throughput at long seqs — but check token-level CPU. Might be tokenizer threads starving GPUs. Try `THREADS=16` and re-run.

raj: also saw periodic spikes ~90s which correlate with our gc script. Consider bumping `cache_eviction_interval` from 60s -> 300s for the experiment.

sara: :white_check_mark: Will rerun with THREADS=16 and `cache_eviction_interval=300s`, plus KERNEL_OVERRIDE where needed. Will update.

devx-bot: When uploading to the Console, mark metadata: environment=private-vpc, customer=acme, hw=8xA100, image=release-20260412 so results are queryable.

mike: awesome. If parity is within 10% of hosted profile we can close this. If not, we'll open a follow-up EPIC to track kernel/driver tuning + infra tweaks. Thanks all.
